name: Siwweschroom
description: Siwweschroom is an Eifel and Rhineland variant of Toepen, a no-trump last-trick game played with four-card hands and aggressive knocking. Players who accumulate seven penalty points are eliminated; the last remaining player wins.
deck: 32-card French pack (10, 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J in each suit)

overview.description: Siwweschroom is an Eifel and Rhineland variant of Toepen, a no-trump last-trick game played with four-card hands and aggressive knocking. Players who accumulate seven penalty points are eliminated; the last remaining player wins.

history.origins: Siwweschroom is documented as a local West German form of Dutch Toepen, especially in the Eifel region and parts of the Rhineland.
timeline: Traditional period: Toepen family games circulate in the Low Countries and neighboring German regions.
Modern documentation: Siwweschroom is recorded as a named regional variant linked to Toepen.
Present: Still played as a social pub and table game under local spellings.
history.cultural: The game sits in a local tradition of noisy, social, risk-taking card play where table image and timing of knocks matter as much as card strength.
history.evolution: Compared with Dutch Toepen, Siwweschroom keeps the same core play but typically omits the theatrical whistle/stand announcements for three or four tens or jacks.

setup.players: 3-8 players in clockwise order. Dealer rotates each hand.
setup.deck: 32-card pack. Rank in every suit is 10 (high), 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J (low). There are no trumps.
setup.dealing: Deal 4 cards to each player. Leader is player to dealer's left.
setup.equipment: Cards plus a score track for penalty points.

rules.objective: Avoid penalty points by winning the fourth (last) trick, or by staying out of expensive losing positions after knocks.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Deal**: Four cards each from a 32-card deck. 2. **Play**: Four tricks are played; players follow suit when able, otherwise discard any card. 3. **Trick winner**: Highest card of the led suit wins and leads next. 4. **Knocking**: After players pick up cards, and at any time during the hand, a player may knock to raise the stake by one life. 5. **Fold or stay**: Opponents may fold (take current loss) or continue. 6. **Hand result**: Winner of trick four avoids loss; others who stayed lose according to the raised stake. 7. **Elimination**: In Siwweschroom, players reaching seven penalty points drop out; last survivor wins.
keyRules: Only the last trick decides the hand winner.
Knocks raise risk for everyone still in.
A player cannot knock and then fold to that same knock.
Siwweschroom end condition is elimination at 7 points, not a fixed 10-point loser rule.

strategy.basic: Preserve your strongest suit card for trick four whenever possible; early tricks are mainly about control of the final lead.
strategy.intermediate: Use folds proactively: conceding one stake is often better than staying into a bad final trick under raised stakes.
strategy.advanced: Time knocks around information edges, such as after seeing opponents commit high cards in a suit you can still dominate on trick four.
tips: Track who can still follow each suit by trick three.
If you cannot realistically win trick four, fold early before another knock lands.
When near elimination, avoid speculative knocks and prioritize survival.

scoring.description: Penalty-life system with variable stake based on knocks. Folding concedes the current stake; staying risks a larger loss if the last trick is lost.
scoring.winCondition: Remain in the game after all opponents have been eliminated at seven penalty points.

synthesis.shortDescription: A German regional Toepen variant where knocks escalate losses and seven points means elimination.
